params.body:
Main went red on the three tests of `VehicleSheetVatChoiceTest`, and not on the five runs before
it. This is the cause, reproduced on demand rather than guessed.

`App\Support\Features` reads the flag table once and keeps it in a static for the rest of the
request, which is right: in production a request is a process. In the suite a process is hundreds
of tests. So a test that writes a flag row hands its answer to every test after it in that process,
long after the transaction that made the row rolled back.

`FeaturesTest` writes rows. `VehicleSheetVatChoiceTest` asks for the classic sheet with
`config(['features.livewire_vehicle_form' => false])`, and got the Livewire one instead, which does
not carry the field it looks for. Hence a page that renders fine and an element that is not on it.

```
phpunit tests/Unit/FeaturesTest.php tests/Feature/VehicleSheetVatChoiceTest.php   3 failures, every time
phpunit tests/Feature/TwoFactorTest.php tests/Feature/VehicleSheetVatChoiceTest.php   green
```

Which tests share a process is a matter of how the parallel runner divides the files, which is why
it came and went and why it always took the whole class with it. `Features::flush()` in
`TestCase::setUp` makes every test start from the same truth. The suite in parallel is green again.
